facts.text: The national cancer roadmap notes that palliative radiotherapy is used less by patients living more than 100 km from the nearest unit, and that outcomes are worse beyond 50 km.
facts.note: Roadmap p. 13. The 100 km finding cites Norwegian data (Åsli 2018); the 50 km finding cites one Ostrobothnia lung cancer study.

facts.text: A systematic review of 29 randomised trials in uncomplicated painful bone metastases: a single session relieves pain as well as a multi-session course (61% vs 62% respond), at the cost of more retreatment (20% vs 8%). Guidelines name 8 Gy as the single dose.

FAST-Forward (4,096 patients): 5 sessions in one week is non-inferior to 15 sessions over three weeks, with a similar level of cancer control at 10 years (breast recurrence 2.1% vs 3.6%). Applies to whole breast or chest wall without nodal radiotherapy.
A single 8 Gy session relieves pain as well as a multi-session course, with more retreatment.
5 sessions in one week is non-inferior to 15 sessions over three weeks for eligible patients.
At Turku University Hospital in 2005-2013, only 7% of radiotherapy courses in patients' last year of life were single-session.
facts.note: Single centre, old and covering all courses, not only bone metastases.

facts.text: Meta-analysis: living 50 km or more from a radiotherapy centre goes with 16% lower odds of receiving palliative radiotherapy (OR 0.84).
Radiotherapy patients often attend daily for several weeks.
Kela paid 364 million euros of travel reimbursement in 2025 for 4.6 million trips; per resident it was highest in Kainuu (157 €) and lowest in Helsinki (23 €).
Patients pay up to 25 € per one-way trip and at most 300 € a year; own-car travel is valued at 0.33 €/km and the overnight allowance is up to 20.18 €.
12 public radiotherapy units serve mainland Finland. Lapland has none: its patients are treated in Oulu.
facts.note: Unit list verified from each unit's public pages; the private Docrates clinic in Helsinki is excluded.

facts.text: 89 municipalities, home to 637,661 people, are more than 100 km by road from their nearest unit.
facts.note: Road distance from each municipality's centre point; population 31 Dec 2025.

facts.text: For part of the population the nearest central hospital is more than 400 km away and the nearest university hospital more than 700 km.
5,232 women were diagnosed with breast cancer in Finland in 2024 (5,204 on the mainland, excluding Åland).

limitations.title: Current schedule mix unknown
limitations.text: How many patients already get the short schedules in Finland is not public. Matka shows it as an adjustable assumption next to what units say on their own pages.

limitations.title: Centre-point distances
limitations.text: Distances run from each municipality's centre point (Wikidata coordinate), not from where patients live. In large municipalities real trips can be much longer or shorter.

limitations.title: Population allocation
limitations.text: Breast cases per municipality are allocated from county counts by female population weighted by age-specific incidence. They are calculated, not registry counts.

limitations.title: Bone counts not public
limitations.text: No citable yearly count of palliative bone radiotherapy courses was found, so the bone lever is shown per patient only.

limitations.title: Routing: sourced catchments, otherwise nearest by drive
limitations.text: Helsinki and Uusimaa are routed to HUS, Pirkanmaa to Tays and Lapland to OYS in Oulu, as their sources state. The other 222 municipalities are routed to the nearest unit by drive time, which is Matka's assumption, not a referral rule. It matters most in Kanta-Häme (municipalities split Turku 4, Lahti 4, Tampere 3, although Tays says it treats most of Kanta-Häme) and Kainuu (split Oulu 5, Kuopio 2, Joensuu 1; no catchment source found). Real referral paths can differ elsewhere too, for example some Satakunta patients are treated in Turku.

limitations.title: Private units excluded
limitations.text: Private clinics (for example Docrates in Helsinki) are excluded; Matka covers the public units only.

limitations.title: Åland excluded
limitations.text: Åland has a separate health system and is left out of the map and totals.

limitations.title: OSRM road data
limitations.text: Drive times come from the public OSRM server on OpenStreetMap data: free-flow driving with no traffic, weather or ferry waits.

limitations.title: Kela cost is a lower bound
limitations.text: Trips are valued at Kela's own-car rate plus the overnight allowance. Taxis cost more, and Kela pays the own-car rate only above the 25 € copayment.

limitations.title: Commuting model
limitations.text: Within the threshold the patient travels daily; beyond it they stay near the unit on weeknights and go home at weekends. Real choices vary (patient hotels, transport by ambulance, family help).

limitations.title: Roadmap distance facts
limitations.text: The roadmap's 100 km finding cites Norwegian data and its 50 km finding one Finnish lung study; they frame the threshold but were not measured for these schedules.

limitations.title: Turku baseline
limitations.text: The 7% single-session figure is from one hospital in 2005-2013 and covers all courses in the last year of life, not only bone metastases.

limitations.title: Eligibility and treatment shares
limitations.text: The shares of breast patients treated with radiotherapy (70%) and eligible for 5 sessions (60%) are assumptions; no citable Finnish figure was found.

limitations.title: Clinical decision
limitations.text: Schedule choice is a clinical decision for each patient. Matka proposes options for clinical teams to evaluate; it does not prescribe.
